 Trail Blazers Face Tough Test vs. Minnesota Timberwolves
 Blazers vs Wolves. Round 1. FIGHT! 
 by Kevin Lawler Nov 16, 2026, 7:57 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 The Portland Trail Blazers start another back-to-back series against a Western Conference contender tonight when they visit the Minnesota Timberwolves
 The Timberwolves (9-4) have barely missed a beat while playing without superstar guard Anthony Edwards, who has missed the last nine games with a knee injury. They had their five-game winning streak snapped on Saturday against the Chicago Bulls, but have otherwise managed to thrive thanks to a balanced scoring attack and the league’s top-rated defense.
 After five seasons as an assistant in Minnesota, Blazers coach Micah Nori knows this stout defense well. How will he choose to attack it? Let’s take a closer look at tonight’s matchup.
 What you need to Know:
 Portland Trail Blazers (9-3) at Minnesota Timberwolves (9-4) - Monday, November 16th - 5:00pm Pacific 
 How to watch: BlazerVision in Oregon and Washington; League Pass everywhere else
 How to listen: Rip City Radio 620AM
 Trail Blazers Injuries: Shaedon Sharpe, Ja Morant, Vít Krejci, Chris Youngblood (Out).
 Timberwolves Injuries: Anthony Edwards, Donte DiVincenzo, Jaylen Clark (Out).
 What to Watch For:
 Easy Points: One way for the Blazers to overcome Rudy Gobert and a stingy Timberwolves defense will be to earn some trips to the foul line. Led by the relentless driving of Deni Avdija, the Blazers take the second most free throws per game in the NBA. And lately, they’ve been very good at actually converting those attempts into points. Over the past three games, the Blazers are a combined 78-of-83 (94%) from the foul line. During that stretch, Avdija has knocked down 21 of his 23 attempts and Damian Lillard has made all 22 of his.
 Balance: Both teams share the ball and get meaningful contributions up and down the roster.
 Avdija and Lillard set the tone for the Blazers offensively and their complimentary styles have really opened up space for several role players to thrive. Toumani Camara (43.6%), Jrue Holiday (42.4%), and Donovan Clingan (43.3%) have all seen significant increases in their three-point shooting percentage compared to last season.
 For the Timberwolves, Edwards averaged 33.3 points through the first four games of the season before his injury. With his production out of the lineup, the Timberwolves have shared the scoring burden. Six other players average in double-figures, led by LaMelo Ball at 18.6 points per game. Ayo Dosunmu’s season average sits at 18.5 points per game, but with a bigger role lately, he has contributed 23 points per game and 41.9% three-point shooting over his past seven games. Jaden McDaniels is on pace for a career-high, chipping in 17 points per game.
 Back-to-Back Back-to-Backs: Robert Williams III played in games on back-to-back nights for the first time as a member of the Blazers last week. With his minutes (16.5 per game) so closely monitored, will this become a more regular occurrence? Will we see him play both games in Minneapolis?
 What Others are Saying:
 Over at Yahoo, Dan Devine wrote about Ball’s impact on the Timberwolves :
 The Wolves generate a higher share of their shots at the rim when LaMelo’s on the floor than when he’s off it. Their 3-point shooting goes through the roof in his minutes, and nearly every member of the team sees a bump in shot quality when playing alongside him.
 The Wolves are more efficient in the half-court when Ball’s at the controls, and they get out in transition way more often with him out there. Minnesota’s team-wide effective field-goal percentage spikes by 6.5% with LaMelo on the floor — the largest on/off split on the team, and one of the largest among all NBA players to log at least 200 minutes this season, according to Cleaning the Glass.
 Coach Nori will be back in a familiar place, but this time, he’ll be patrolling the sidelines in front of the visiting bench. When he accepted the job with the Blazers, Timberwolves coach Chris Finch had nothing but praise for his former assistant . In a June story by Joe Freeman at The Oregonian, Finch said:
 He’ll be amazing. He’s such a deep foundation and understands all angles of this job. He’s ready for it. He’s elite in his relationship-building. I know he’ll fit right in in a situation where it’s really promising. I think it’s going to be a perfect match.
